---
title: "Posterior dependence and pairwise comparisons"
subtitle: "1.9 · two jointly normal posteriors; dependence after the postrank theory book, ch. 9 and 24"
description: "Effect of correlation on direction probabilities under a bivariate normal posterior distribution."
---

Two units with fixed marginal posteriors can still move together. Under joint normality, correlation rescales the spread of $\theta_A - \theta_B$ without changing which direction exceeds one half.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Correlation .50.** Difference SD narrows from .283 to .200; $\pi_{AB}$ rises from .760 to .841.
- **Independent.** Correlation 0 draws a circle (SD .283, $\pi_{AB}$ = .760).
- **Correlation .95.** Difference SD narrows to .0632; $\pi_{AB}$ rises above .999.
- **Correlation −.95.** Difference SD widens to .395; $\pi_{AB}$ falls to .694.
- **Shared prior mean.** Estimates .30, .10 (SE .20, prior SD .10, prior-mean SD .50) give ρ = .645, SD .126, $\pi_{AB}$ = .624 (vs. .212, .575 independent); prior-mean SD 0 gives unit SDs .0894 and $\pi_{AB}$ = .624.

<details>
<summary>Where the correlation comes from</summary>

Given the prior mean, each posterior mean keeps the share $k = \text{prior SD}^2/(\text{prior SD}^2 + \text{SE}^2)$ of its estimate, independently. Both posterior variables depend on the uncertain prior mean, so their covariance is $(1 - k_A)(1 - k_B)\,v$, with $v$ the prior mean's variance given both estimates (theory book, ch. 24); with equal SEs the shared part cancels from the difference. `postrank` takes such posteriors as joint draws, or as normal laws averaged over the prior mean (`postrank_mixture_coefficients()`).
</details>

Standalone: [embed/correlated-units.html](../../embed/correlated-units.html) (`?corr=-.50` or `?preset=shared-mean&meanSd=0`). Related: [Pairwise posterior direction probabilities](two-units.qmd) (1.8); [Marginal summaries and joint direction probabilities](beyond-normal.qmd) (1.10).
